overview: A federal judge has issued a ruling restricting homeland security field operations aimed at unearthing voter fraud across multiple states including California. In commercial real estate news, Ken Griffin secured a massive construction loan for a Manhattan office tower, while Los Angeles multifamily sales saw a notable jump. Locally in San Francisco, the husband of a slain UCSF social worker is suing the city over inadequate security at the hospital. Meanwhile, developments in Hawaii include a board vote for a new Office of Hawaiian Affairs CEO and a community battle over a luxury housing proposal in Princeville.

items.title: Judge Restricts D.H.S. Field Operations Aimed at Unearthing Voter Fraud
items.summary: A judge blocked homeland security agents from conducting field interviews in nine states, including California, regarding noncitizen voter registration.

items.title: How Mark Zuckerberg Pushed Meta to Shield Him From California’s Proposed Wealth Tax
items.summary: Mark Zuckerberg told Meta's board he planned to sell his Silicon Valley home to avoid a proposed California wealth tax, prompting a stock structure change.

items.title: U.S. and Israel Draw Up Plans for Renewed Strikes on Iran After Elections
items.summary: The United States and Israel are drawing up plans for renewed strikes on Iran following elections.

items.title: Ken Griffin Seals $3.3B Construction Loan for Manhattan Office Tower
items.summary: Ken Griffin secured a 3.3 billion dollar construction loan for a Midtown Manhattan office tower as part of a joint venture.

items.title: Canadian Investor Buys Two Hotels in Palm Beach County for More Than $48M
items.summary: Canadian investor Brasswater purchased two Hampton Inns hotels in Palm Beach County for more than 48 million dollars.

items.title: Mexican Eatery Casa Carmen to Open Third Manhattan Location
items.summary: Mexican eatery Casa Carmen signed a 15-year lease for its third Manhattan location in Midtown East.

items.title: L.A. Multifamily Sales Jump 44%
items.summary: Los Angeles County multifamily investment sales increased after the third quarter while rents and occupancy remained stuck in neutral.

items.title: Husband of slain UCSF social worker sues city over ‘woefully inadequate security’
items.summary: The husband of a slain UCSF social worker is suing San Francisco over woefully inadequate security at S.F. General.

items.title: Ken Fulk is selling his beloved ‘Tree House’ for $7.9 million — and moving to a new hill
items.summary: Designer Ken Fulk is selling his Clarendon Heights redwood midcentury home for 7.9 million dollars and moving across the city.

items.title: Meet the District 8 candidates: Should S.F. expand rent control?
items.summary: District 8 supervisor candidates in San Francisco are sharing their thoughts on whether to expand rent control.

items.title: Looks Like OHA Has A New CEO
items.summary: A vote finalizing Todd Apo's appointment as the new CEO of the Office of Hawaiian Affairs is expected on Thursday.

items.title: Bodyboarder, 32, rescued off Hapuna Beach
items.summary: Hawaii County firefighters rescued a 32-year-old bodyboarder after strong currents swept him more than a mile offshore from Hapuna Beach.

items.title: Lines Drawn In Princeville Battle: Golf Course Views Vs. Luxury Development
items.summary: Lawsuits have been filed and police called as a global investment company pushes a luxury housing proposal in Princeville.

items.title: So What’s With All These Charter And Constitutional Amendments?
items.summary: Voters are evaluating charter amendments for Honolulu, Hawaiʻi, Maui, and Kauaʻi counties alongside state constitutional amendments.
